name: CUORICINO
summary: CUORICINO was the cryogenic tellurium-130 predecessor of CUORE at Gran Sasso. It demonstrated an array of massive bolometers and established the background and construction experience used for later CUORE detectors.
detection_principle: TeO2 crystals served simultaneously as isotope source and calorimeter. Neutron-transmutation-doped germanium thermistors measured temperature pulses produced by particle energy deposition.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final CUORICINO search reported no neutrinoless signal and constrained the 130Te half-life.

results.summary: The final CUORICINO search reported no neutrinoless signal and constrained the 130Te half-life.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
